source_text:
Fragmenta in Matthaeum
1 Mt 21, 23 Τοῖς δολεροῖς μὴ προσιοῦσιν εἰς τὸ μαθεῖν ἄκαιρον ἀναπτύσσειν
τὰ βαθύτερα.
2 μτ 21, 28–32 Ἄνθρωπός τις εἶχεν δύο υἱοὺς καὶ ὁ μὲν πρῶτός ἐστιν τὰ ἔθνη,
οὓς ὁ θεὸς ὁ κοινὸς πατὴρ πρώτους ἐκάλεσεν· τὸν γὰρ διδακτὸν καὶ φυσικὸν νόμον
ταῖς διανοίαις ἐγκατασπείρας ἔδωκε κήρυκας τὰ ὁρώμενα, ἀλλ' ἡ τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτῶν
εὐταξία συνεχύθη ἐπὶ ξύλα καὶ λίθους· «εἶπαν «, γὰρ «τῷ ξύλῳ· πατήρ μου εἶ σύ «.
διὸ οὐκ ἠνέσχοντο κωλυόμενοι· εἶπον γὰρ οὐκ οἴδαμεν τὸν κύριον. οὗτοι οὖν
μεταμεληθέντες ὕστερον ἀπῆλθον εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα.
thought_title: The first son as the Gentiles
orientation: Theophilus is opening his commentary on Matthew 21:23 and 21:28–32, explaining that the first son in the parable represents the Gentiles, whom God called first.
pass_a_gloss: To the deceitful who do not come to learn, it is untimely to unfold the deeper things. A certain man had two sons, and the first is the Gentiles, whom God the common Father called first; for having sown the teachable and natural law in their minds, he gave the visible things as heralds, but the good order of their soul was poured out onto wood and stones; for they said to the wood: you are my father. Therefore they did not endure being hindered; for they said: we do not know the Lord. These, then, having repented later, went away into the vineyard.

choices.english: it is untimely to unfold the deeper things
choices.why: Keeps the impersonal force of the Greek adjective with infinitive, preserving the judgment that unfolding is untimely for the deceitful.
rejected: it is not the time to unfold the deeper things
unfolding the deeper things is untimely

choices.why: Matches the glossary rendering exactly and preserves the two adjectives as coordinate modifiers of law.
rejected: the natural law that can be taught

choices.term: ἡ τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτῶν εὐταξία συνεχύθη
choices.english: the good order of their soul was poured out
choices.why: Uses the glossary term 'good order' and renders συνεχύθη literally as 'was poured out' to keep the image of disorder being poured onto wood and stones.
rejected: the good order of their soul was confused
their soul's good order was poured out

choices.english: they did not endure being hindered
choices.why: Keeps the middle voice of ἀνέχομαι with the passive participle, preserving the sense that they refused to tolerate hindrance.
rejected: they did not put up with being hindered
they could not bear being hindered

choices.why: Renders μεταμέλομαι as 'repent' per the glossary's μετανοέω sense, and keeps the aorist participle with the temporal adverb.

bible_refs.note: Τοῖς δολεροῖς μὴ προσιοῦσιν εἰς τὸ μαθεῖν
τῷ ξύλῳ· πατήρ μου εἶ σύ

pass_b_english: It is untimely to unfold the deeper things to deceitful people who do not come to learn (Matthew 21:23).

A man had two sons, and the first son is the Gentiles, whom God the common Father called first. For he sowed the teachable and natural law in their minds and gave the visible creation as heralds, but the good order of their soul was poured out onto wood and stones. For they said to the wood, “You are my father.” Therefore they did not endure being hindered, for they said, “We do not know the Lord.” So these, having regretted it later, went away into the vineyard (Matthew 21:28–32).

problems.source_quote: «εἶπαν «, γὰρ «τῷ ξύλῳ· πατήρ μου εἶ σύ «
problems.why: The brief marks this as Gentiles' speech, not Jeremiah citation; no OT book name in source.
problems.fix: Remove '(Jeremiah 2:27)' or mark as Gentiles' words per brief's voice marking.

problems.source_quote: εἶπον γὰρ οὐκ οἴδαμεν τὸν κύριον
problems.why: Source has no book name; this is likely continuing Gentiles' speech, not Exodus citation.
problems.fix: Remove '(Exodus 5:2)' or treat as Gentiles' words, not scripture citation.

problems.why: μεταμέλομαι is 'regretted/changed mind', not μετανοέω 'repented'; brief distinguishes these.
problems.fix: having regretted it later, or having changed their minds later
problems.ruling: μεταμεληθέντες from μεταμέλομαι means 'regretted/changed mind,' distinct from μετανοέω 'repented'; brief distinguishes these.

edits.old: For they said to the wood, “You are my father” (Jeremiah 2:27).
edits.new: For they said to the wood, “You are my father.”

edits.old: Therefore they did not endure being hindered, for they said, “We do not know the Lord” (Exodus 5:2).
edits.new: Therefore they did not endure being hindered, for they said, “We do not know the Lord.”

edits.old: So these, having repented later, went away into the vineyard
edits.new: So these, having regretted it later, went away into the vineyard

fixed: Removed '(Jeremiah 2:27)' as the source has no book name and the brief marks this as the Gentiles' speech.
Removed '(Exodus 5:2)' as the source has no book name and this continues the Gentiles' speech.
Changed 'having repented later' to 'having regretted it later' to distinguish μεταμέλομαι from μετανοέω.

last_rejected.quote: Therefore they did not endure being hindered
last_rejected.why: οὐκ ἠνέσχοντο means 'they did not accept/consent to'; 'did not endure' misreads the verb.
last_rejected.fix: Therefore they did not consent when hindered
last_rejected.ruling: ἠνέσχοντο is aorist middle of ἀνέχομαι, meaning 'endure, bear, put up with'; 'did not endure' is well within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: For they said to the wood, "You are my father."
last_rejected.source_quote: «εἶπαν», γὰρ «τῷ ξύλῳ· πατήρ μου εἶ σύ»
last_rejected.why: English hides that γὰρ is inside quotation marks, making it seem like authorial comment not Gentiles' words.
last_rejected.fix: For they said, "To the wood: You are my father."
last_rejected.ruling: Greek punctuation is editorial; γὰρ connects the quotation to the argument regardless of mark placement. Meaning is preserved.

last_rejected.why: μεταμέλομαι means repent/regret, but context demands 'repented' per glossary and argument.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Regretted' is within normal range of μεταμεληθέντες; no meaning change or reader misleading. Mere preference.
